Indicators that rose or fell between two years for one country

Source: R/fct_change.R
indicator_change.Rd

Compares every indicator a country has a value for in both years, for the Change (%) tab, and splits them into two tables: the ones that increased from year1 to year2 and the ones that decreased, each sorted by percent change (largest change first). The percent change is (value2 - value1) / |value1| * 100; it is undefined when the year1 value is 0, so those indicators are left out of both tables (their names are kept in the zero_base element). Indicators that did not change are in neither table.

Rates of change ("annual %", "% change", "growth", e.g. "GDP growth (annual %)", "Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)", "... (% change from 1990)") are left out by default: a percent change of a growth rate is not meaningful (a rate going from -0.01 to 1.7 reads as +17,000%). include_rates = TRUE keeps them.

For indicators that are themselves percentages (e.g. "Urban population (% of total population)") the percent change is relative to the old percentage, not a difference in percentage points; the Change column gives the plain difference.

Usage

indicator_change(
  mfi,
  country,
  year1,
  year2,
  include_rates = FALSE,
  include_sign_change = FALSE
)

Arguments

mfi

Data frame of World Bank indicator values (long format, with Country Name, Indicator Name, Year, value columns).

country

Character. Country name, as in Country Name.

year1, year2

Numeric or character. The two years to compare.

include_rates

Logical. Keep the rate-of-change indicators (names containing "annual %", "% change" or "growth"); FALSE (default) leaves them out.

include_sign_change

Logical. Keep indicators whose value changed sign between the two years (e.g. net FDI inflows from -8 million to +6.7 billion): their percent change is not meaningful (+82,000%). FALSE (default) leaves them out; either way they are listed in sign_change.

Value

A list with increased and decreased (data frames with the columns Indicator, one named after each year with its value, Change and Change %), zero_base (indicators left out because their year1 value is 0) and sign_change (indicators whose value changed sign; left out of the tables unless include_sign_change = TRUE). Stops with an error when the country has no data in either year.

Examples

res <- indicator_change(mfi, country = "Greece", year1 = 2000, year2 = 2020)
head(res$increased)
#>                                                                             Indicator         2000         2020       Change Change %
#> 1     International tourism, expenditures for passenger transport items (current US$) 6.000000e+06 6.020000e+08 5.960000e+08  9933.33
#> 2                                                     Children out of school, primary 4.740000e+02 2.396600e+04 2.349200e+04  4956.12
#> 3                                    Children out of school (% of primary school age) 7.517000e-02 3.727260e+00 3.652090e+00  4858.44
#> 4 Electricity production from renewable sources, excluding hydroelectric (% of total) 8.376205e-01 2.945185e+01 2.861423e+01  3416.13
#> 5        Electricity production from renewable sources, excluding hydroelectric (kWh) 4.510000e+08 1.421081e+10 1.375981e+10  3050.96
#> 6         International tourism, receipts for passenger transport items (current US$) 4.300000e+07 1.178000e+09 1.135000e+09  2639.53
head(res$decreased)
#>                                                            Indicator          2000          2020        Change Change %
#> 1                  Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) (current LCU) -5.720000e+09 -1.612600e+10 -1.040600e+10  -181.92
#> 2 Carbon dioxide (CO2) net fluxes from LULUCF - Other Land (Mt CO2e) -1.258600e+00 -3.237100e+00 -1.978500e+00  -157.20
#> 3                     Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) (% of GDP) -4.200904e+00 -9.625192e+00 -5.424288e+00  -129.12
#> 4                        Fossil fuel energy consumption (% of total)  9.438860e+01  0.000000e+00 -9.438860e+01  -100.00
